note: India's largest banks are the State Bank of India (whose cards SBI Card issues), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. SBI Card is written here; HDFC Bank's and ICICI Bank's terms weren't reached in this pass. SBI Card's most important terms and conditions (read again 2026-10-30): every card in its fee table is written (the Vyapaar Unnati and SimplySAVE Merchant cards, for merchants, aren't), each with its one-time annual fee at issue (written as the issue fee; none where the table says NIL) and its renewal fee each year from the second, waived where the table states spending of a figure in the preceding year (a lakh is 100,000 rupees; the Bank of Maharashtra SimplySAVE renewal printed '4,99' is read as 499), the SBI Card Unnati's renewal fee from its fifth year (written as waived for four years); the SimplySAVE SBI Card this file has held since 2026-10-29 (499, waived on 1 lakh) is among them. Finance charges up to 3.75% a month (45% a year) on unsecured cards, written at that figure, and 2.75% a month on the Shaurya (defence) and secured cards (the PRIME NRI Secured), on purchases and cash; interest-free 20 to 50 days on purchases when the previous balance was paid in full, written as 50; a cash advance 2.5%, at least 500 rupees; the minimum payment 2% of the balance plus all GST, instalments, fees, charges and finance charges and any over-limit amount (written as 2% with the interest added; the fees aren't); over the limit 2.5% of the excess, at least 600 rupees; a dishonoured payment 2% of the payment, at least 500 rupees (written as 500); spending in another currency 3.5%, 3% on the MILES, 2.5% on the MILES PRIME and 1.99% on the AURUM, ELITE, PRIME NRI Secured, Tata Neu Infinity and MILES ELITE (read as the SBI Card ELITE and ELITE Advantage for 'Elite'; the partner banks' ELITE cards are written at 3.5%); GST at 18% on all fees, interest and charges (Haryana's 9% central and 9% state are the same 18%). The late payment charge is a step by the amount due (nothing up to 100 rupees, then 100, 500, 750, 950, 1,100 and 1,300 above 50,000, with 100 more after two missed cycles), which the form doesn't hold, so it isn't written; nor are the 250-rupee cash payment fee, the 1% utility, education and wallet fees above their thresholds, or the 99-rupee redemption fee. Wave 4 (2026-10-30): Axis Bank, among India's three largest private banks and card issuers, is added; HDFC Bank's key fact statement cum most important terms (updated 15 December 2025) was fetched from hdfc.bank.in, but its card fee table's merged cells can't be read card by card from the PDF in this pass, so no HDFC card is written; ICICI Bank's card page carries a captcha (2026-10-30). Axis Bank's Key Fact Sheet for its credit cards (last updated 8 October 2026), a PDF whose tables were checked by eye against the rendered page, read 2026-10-30: each retail, partnership, affluent and secured card's joining fee (written as the issue fee, the first year's fee being the joining fee, so the annual fee is written waived the first year) and annual fee, with the spending in the preceding year that waives it (a lakh is 100,000 rupees); interest 55.55% a year on most cards, 42.58% on the MAGNUS, OLYMPUS and RESERVE, 12.68% on the PRIMUS and 49.36% on the secured cards (the annualised figures of monthly rates, 3.75% a month in its worked example; written as effective yearly rates); a cash withdrawal 2.5%, at least 500 rupees (2%, at least 300, on the OLYMPUS; none on the MAGNUS, PRIMUS and RESERVE); over the limit 2.5% of the excess, at least 500 (none on the PRIMUS and OLYMPUS); a returned payment 2% of the payment, at least 500 (written as 500; 350 on the OLYMPUS; none on the PRIMUS); the foreign transaction fee 3.5% (none on the PRIMUS and SCAPIA, 1.5% RESERVE, 2% MAGNUS, 1.8% OLYMPUS, 2.5% IndiGo Premium); 20 to 50 days free of interest, written as 50; the minimum amount due 2% of the balance plus fees, interest and taxes (its worked example), written as 2% with the interest added; charges before GST, at 18% in its worked example on fees and on interest, written as a tax on both. The PRIMUS's joining fee of 5 lakh is for cards issued after 31 July 2024. Not written: the late payment fee, a step by the amount outstanding (nothing below 500 rupees, then 500, 750, 1,200 and 1,300 above 50,000, with 100 more after two missed minimums), which the form doesn't hold; the MAGNUS for Burgundy and Burgundy Private cards, open only to the bank's Burgundy clients; the waivers for Burgundy salary or savings account holders and for HON and SEN status members, conditions the game doesn't check; the legacy cards no longer on sale (Visa Gold, Visa Silver, Buzz, My Wings, My Choice, Titanium, Platinum, Signature, Infinite); the rent, education, wallet, fuel, utility and gaming fees.
